DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 30 s. 2022 April 26, 2022 MR. HOMER R. JAJALLA Secretary to the Sanggunian Sangguniang Bayan of Mahinog Province of Camiguin Dear Mr. Jajalla: This pertains to your letter dated IO January 2022 requesting for an opinion on the interpretation of Sec. 336 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Govemment Code". Section 336, of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code", provides as follows: "Funds shall be available exclusively for the specific purpose for which they have been appropriated. No ordinance shall be passed authorizing any transfer of appropriations from one item to another. However, the local chief executive or the presiding officer of the Sanggunian concemed may, by ordinance, be authorized to augment any item in the approved annual budget for their respective offices from savings in other items within the same expense class of their respective appropriations. " Per the letter, your interpretation to the above stated provision is quoted as follows: "The afore-quoted provision of law clearly requires the passing of an ordinance before an item can be augmented from savings in another item. In this case, there was no ordinance authorizing the acting mayor to augment the said item of appropriation. " (Emphasis Supplied) To such interpretation we cannot agree without qualification. The general rule that is plainly laid down by the second sentence of Section 336, LGC, is that no item can be augmented by transferring appropriations from one item to another and no ordinance shall be passed authorizing the same. By way of an exception to this general rule, the only augmentation that is allowed is when the item to be augmented by savings is within the same expense class of the item from which the savings are derived, and that augmentation is possible only through an ordinance. Thus, the letter-senders interpretation is true only insofar as the exception to the general rule on budget augmentation applies. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Further, the following queries were submitted, as quoted. 1. "Whether or not the acting mayor violated Section 336 of Republic Act No 7160, and can be held administratively, civilly or criminally liable, for issuing an executive order to augment the appropriation for Performance-based Bonus/PRAlSE, instead of obtaining the requisite authority from the Sangguniang Bayan through an ordinance? 2. Whether or not the disbursements of funds were legal in light of Section 305 (a) of R.A. 7160 which requires the passing of an appropriation ordinance before public funds can be paid out of local treasury? 3 Whether or not the use of savings to augment certain items of appropriation requires an ordinance by the Sangguniang bayan or only an executive order by mayor? 4. If there was a violation of Section 336 of R.A. 7160 and Section 305 (a). of R.A. 7160, who are the officials liable for such violation, if any? 5. What will happen to the disbursements if found in violation of Section 336 and For the the acting Mayor shall be deemed to have violated Section 336 of R.A. No. 7160 only if the augmentation was not authorized by an ordinance duly enacted by the Sanggunian. The issuance of an Executive Order for that matter is of no moment as said issuance should be anchored to an ordinance as required by law. For the second query, the disbursement of funds pursuant to an augmentation of appropriation authorized by a mere Executive Order was illegal in the light of Section 305 (a) of R.A. No. 7160 which provides that "(n)o money shall be paid out of local treasury except in pursuance of an appropriations ordinance or law". For the third query, we reiterate that an ordinance is required for the augmentation allowed under the third sentence of Section 336, LGC. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 004- 06, dated 07 February 2006, we have enumerated the requisites for this kind of budget augmentation to be valid, viz: "For a realignment to be valid, the following requisites must concur: I. There must be an ordinance authorizing the Local Chief Executive or the Presiding Officer to augment any item; 2. The item to be augmented is limited to their respective offices; and 3. The funds from where the "augmentation" should come from should be the savings in the other items within the same expense class of each office's respective appropriations " DILG Opinion No. 28, s. of 2020, cited the explanation of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) in the Budget Operations Manual for Local Government, 2016 Edition, to wit: "The ordinance will give the omnibus authority to the LCE or the Presiding Officer of the Sanggunian to augment any item in the approved annual budget for their respective offices from savings in other items within the same expense class of their respective appropriations. " (Emphasis Supplied) Page 2 of 3

For the fourth query, it is the official who augmented an item in violation of Section 336 of the LGC who will be primarily liable. All other officials' or employees' liåbility in respect thereto will depend on the circumstances and their participation as may be determined by the proper court. As for the fifth query, it is very likely that the disbursements surrounding an invalid augmentation will be subjected to Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM) of the Commission on Audit (COA) and the latter's decision as to what will happen to the involved funds will depend on its assessment of the justifications provided in response to the AOM. In case of failure to justify, it may be subjected to Notices of Suspension and Disallowance where the responsible officials and employees may be held liable. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse ry for Local Government LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/kvb ARNEL M. AGABE Regional Director, DILG-Region X Km3 Fr. W.F. Masterson Avenue, Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City, Misamis Oriental Page 3 of 3
